rationale: This is a tiny (317 LOC, 7 functions, ~4.8 KB text) compute-bound MD5 kernel where virtually all runtime sits in the hot md5_process round loop (3 KB of a 4.8 KB binary), so the table privileges low-cost arithmetic and layout transforms while suppressing overhead-heavy control-flow insertion: SUB gets the highest security/diversity weights because MD5 is dominated by add/xor/rotate arithmetic that instruction substitution obfuscates cheaply with near-zero risk; FLA is kept at moderate weight since flattening md5_process's round structure yields strong resistance and the function is small enough that the dispatcher overhead is bounded, but its RuntimeCost weight is raised so the hottest loop is not aggressively flattened; BCF is effectively throttled (high RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights) because bogus-chain execution taxes every iteration of the hot loop and would balloon a 4.8 KB binary; SPLIT and IBR are inexpensive diversity boosters best applied to the larger cold functions (main, md5_finish) to break up structural signatures without touching throughput; ICALL is penalized for runtime and correctness risk since the program has no natural indirect-call structure and added indirection only slows dispatch; and IGV is a cheap global-variable hiding layer well suited to MD5's state/tables, contributing diversity at negligible size cost in a program where the whole binary must stay small.
